title: Gotdocs document frontmatter
$comment: NOTHING VALIDATES AGAINST THIS FILE AT RUNTIME. The gotdocs CLI is Python 3.9+ stdlib only (no jsonschema, no PyYAML) and re-implements these rules natively in tools/gotdocs/frontmatter.py. This schema exists as the precise, machine-readable statement of the frontmatter format: use it for editor integration (VS Code yaml.schemas, JetBrains, Zed), for third-party tooling, and as the reference when changing the native validator. If you change one, change the other in the same commit.

id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier, unique repo-wide. Used by `gotdocs verify <id>` and by agents to reference the doc. Renaming it is a breaking change for anything that cites it.

title.description: Human-readable title. Rendered as the page heading by downstream static site generators.

type.description: Document kind. Controls which template scaffolds it, how it is grouped in .gotdocs/INDEX.md, and which Claude skill maintains it. 'decision' is an architecture decision record: it lives under the decisions root, is named NNNN-slug.md, uses the decision status enum, and is searched by `gotdocs why`.

summary.description: One sentence. This exact string is what lands in .gotdocs/INDEX.md and index.json, so it is the only text an agent sees before deciding whether to open the file. Must be specific enough to make that decision. Limit mirrors config.max_summary_chars.
examples: Vendored stdlib-only CLI that computes which docs a code change impacts and enforces freshness.

covers.description: Repo-relative glob patterns naming the code this document describes. A change touching any of these paths makes this doc impacted, and an impacted doc must be edited or re-verified in the same change. May be an empty list for docs that describe no specific code (policies, glossaries).

items.$comment: Patterns are repo-relative and /-separated with no leading './' or '/'. Supported syntax: '*' (not crossing /), '**' (crossing /), '?', '[abc]', '[a-z]', '[!abc]'; a pattern with no '/' and no '**' matches the basename at any depth; a trailing '/' means that directory and everything under it.

status.description: Lifecycle state, from one of two disjoint enums chosen by 'type'. Every type except 'decision' uses current | draft | deprecated: 'current' is enforced normally, 'draft' is a work in progress, and a 'deprecated' doc is reported when edited so it gets deleted rather than quietly maintained. A 'decision' uses proposed | accepted | rejected | superseded; only 'accepted' records are listed in .gotdocs/INDEX.md and only they are searched by `gotdocs why` without --all. The native validator in tools/gotdocs/index.py enforces the per-type split, which JSON Schema cannot express in one enum.
status.$comment: See allOf below for the conditional that a schema-aware editor applies.

updated.description: ISO 8601 calendar date (YYYY-MM-DD) the content was last meaningfully changed. Written by `gotdocs verify`.

owners.description: Who to ask. Free-form handles; '@name' for people, '@org/team' for teams.

tags.description: Lowercase keywords for grouping and search.

verified_at.description: Git commit sha (short or long, lowercase hex) at which `covers` and the content were last confirmed accurate. Written by `gotdocs verify`. An impacted doc is satisfied when this equals the head sha of the change set.

symptoms.description: Decision records only. Observable behaviour this record explains, one phrase per entry, written the way somebody would describe it when they hit it. This is the entire search corpus for `gotdocs why`, and it is deliberately kept OUT of .gotdocs/INDEX.md: that file is loaded into an agent's context on every session and must stay small.
examples: a POST is retried exactly twice and then fails fast

decided_on.description: Decision records only. The date the decision was made, which is not the date the file was last touched ('updated').

supersedes.description: Decision records only. Ids of the records this one replaces. The link must be bidirectional: each named record must list this record under 'superseded_by'. `gotdocs lint` enforces both halves.

superseded_by.description: Decision records only. Ids of the records that replaced this one. A record with a non-empty 'superseded_by' must have status 'superseded', and vice versa.

additionalPropertiesRationale.$comment: additionalProperties is intentionally true: unknown keys are pass-through. The gotdocs frontmatter writer preserves every line it does not own byte-for-byte, so downstream static site generators may add their own keys (sidebar_position, slug, draft, weight, layout, nav_order, description, date, aliases, toc, hide, ...) without gotdocs stripping, reordering or rejecting them. Values must still be expressible in the supported YAML subset: scalars, inline flow lists of scalars, or block lists of scalars. Nested maps and multiline scalars are lint errors regardless of key.
